M-Centrality

Source: R/centrality-batch69.R
centrality_m_centrality.Rd

M-centrality (Ibnoulouafi et al. 2018) mixes the coreness of a node with a local variation of degree among its neighbors, by weights taken from the entropy of the two terms over the network: $$M_i = \mu K_s(i) + (1 - \mu) \Delta D_i, \qquad \Delta D_i = k_i \sum_{j \in N(i)} \frac{|k_j - k_i|}{\sum_{l \in N(i)} k_l}, \qquad \mu = \frac{1 - E_1}{2 - E_1 - E_2},$$ with \(k\) the degree, \(K_s\) the coreness and \(E_1\), \(E_2\) the entropies of the shares \(K_s(j)/\sum K_s\) and \(\Delta D_j / \sum \Delta D\), divided by \(\ln n\).

Usage

centrality_m_centrality(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality, such as normalized.

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order.

Details

The measure is computed on the simple undirected skeleton of the network, so direction, weights, loops and parallel edges are ignored. The absolute value covers the whole fraction of the source's equation (7); the Centrality Zoo prints the term without it, which makes it negative for hubs. When the weights of equation (11) have no value the two terms are weighted 1/2 each (owner decision 2026-11-26): on a regular network, and on any network where every node's neighbors share its degree, \(\Delta D\) is 0 at every node and its shares are 0/0; the same applies when both entropies are 1, on a network without edges and on a one-node network. With equal weights such a network scores half its coreness. An isolated node has an empty neighbor sum, \(\Delta D = 0\), and coreness 0. The source prints no score; the implementation reproduces the values and the weight \(\mu = 0.37263\) that two source audits computed independently on the Krackhardt kite (10 of 10). On four test networks no existing measure has a mean Kendall correlation above 0.56 with the score (centrality_nwrank 0.555); with the degree the correlation is 0.00 to 0.84 and with the coreness -0.09 to 0.72. normalized = TRUE divides the scores by their maximum.

References

Ibnoulouafi, A., El Haziti, M. and Cherifi, H. (2018). M-centrality: identifying key nodes based on global position and local degree variation. Journal of Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Experiment, 2018(7), 073407. doi:10.1088/1742-5468/aace08 .

See also

centrality_coreness, centrality_degree, centrality.

Examples

centrality_m_centrality(regulation_net)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>  0.3703704  1.1250000  2.2702703  1.3548387  0.5769231  0.5357143  1.3333333 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>  0.8333333  0.9090909  0.8333333
